The present claim petition arises out of the Detailed Accident Report (DAR as per directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Rajesh Tyagi Vs. Jaibir Singh; II(2010) ACC 781) filed by the Investigating Officer upon which a reasoned responses have been filed by all the respondents and the same has been taken up for determination of just and reasonable compensation payable to the LRs of the deceased victim Suraj aged 21 years who is stated to have unfortunately died in the road accident.

sentences.text: The claim is being perused on behalf of LRs of deceased to elucidate the facts and circumstances pertaining to the deceased.
MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 2.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 01.01.2019, deceased namely Suraj (aged about 21 years) was coming towards the site of work i.e. inside the B.G. Sirke Company, Narela, Delhi on foot.

At about 2:45 PM, when he reached in front of Mansa Mata Devi Mandir, B.G. Sirke Construction Company, Narela, Delhi, all of a sudden, offending vehicle (Truck)
bearing registration no. HR74-0211 which was being driven by its driver/respondent no. 1 at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from Singhu Border side and hit the deceased with a great force, as a result of which, he fell down on the road and sustained serious/grievous injuries all over his body, which resulted into unfortunate and premature death.
He was immediately taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, where he was medically examined.
Postmortem of the deceased was conducted at BJRM Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi.
A case U/s 279/304A IPC was registered at PS. Alipur vide FIR No. 01/19 with regard to the accident in question.

The petitioners (parents of deceased) have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was duly insured with respondent no. 3/Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., at the time of accident in question.

9. I have heard Ld. Counsels for the parties at length and perused the record including the pleadings of the documents, appreciated evidence led on record and examined the legal position applicable to the facts of the present case.

The issue wise determination is as under:-
10.
The onus to prove, the aforesaid issue was placed on the petitioners.

To prove the said issue, the petitioners have examined PW2 Sh. Ram Raksha who deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW2/A) that on 01.01.2019, he was working in a Pit at Pocket - 13, site in BG Sirke Company.
He further deposed that on the said day between 2:45 PM to 3:00 PM, he received a call from his brother namely Suraj (deceased herein) who wanted to meet him there.
He further deposed that after receiving his call, he came out from the pit and saw that his brother Suraj was coming on foot towards him, with due care and caution from Pocket - 13 main gate side.

He deposed that when his deceased brother Suraj reached in front of Mansa Mata Devi Mandir, BG Sirke Construction Company, Narela, Delhi when all of a sudden, offending vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no.
HR74-2011, which was being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, at a very MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 high speed, came from Singhu Border side and was coming inside the BG Sirke Company, hit his brother Suraj with great force, due to which,
he fell down on the road and sustained serious/grievous injuries all over his body, which resulted his unfortunate and premature death.
He categorically deposed that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1.
He further deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle came out from his vehicle and offending vehicle was seized from the spot.

He has relied upon copy of his Aadhaar Card as Ex. PW2/1 and copy of his office identity card as Ex. PW2/2.
11.

The aforesaid witness (PW2) was then subjected to the cross examination by the Ld. Counsel for insurance company where he deposed that his working hours during his employment were from 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
He further deposed that he was working in a pit which was about 50 feet deep when he received a call on his mobile from the deceased.
He further deposed that deceased did not disclose any urgency even after his asking and just asked him that he wanted to meet him.
He further deposed that he did not have any documentary proof to show that his deceased brother was also employed in B.G. Sirke Company.
He denied the suggestion that neither he nor his deceased brother were employed in the said company or that the document Ex. PW2/2 was a false and fabricated document.
He deposed that the deceased was about 50 meters away from him at the time of accident.

He further deposed that the accident took place about 200 meters inside the MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 company premises from the public road outside the company and there were number of persons walking near by and around the deceased at the time of accident.
He further deposed that there were number of vehicles plying on the road where the accident took place at the time of accident.

He further deposed that both the left side wheels of the offending vehicle had run over the body of deceased and explained that firstly, the left front portion of the vehicle had stuck against the deceased.
He further deposed that he did not lodge any police report in writing and he did not make a call to the police through his mobile phone and that some unknown person called the police.

He denied the suggestion that nobody in his presence Ramlaut And Ors (Lrs Of Suraj) vs Badree Mandal on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88377419/

He denied the suggestion that he is a planted witness or that he was not present on spot due to which he did not tell anything regarding the manner of accident to the police or that due to which he did not lodge any complaint against the police officials.

He deposed that the offending vehicle was carrying bricks at the time of accident for delivery at the construction site of the company and that the offending vehicle used to come frequently at site and was having Haryana number.

PW2, during further cross-examination failed to furnish any knowledge about 4-5 persons who took the deceased to SRHC hospital in the ambulance and reached at SRHC hospital at about 6- 6:30 PM on the day of accident.
He further deposed that the deceased was declared dead about 15 minutes, after their reaching the hospital.

During MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 further cross, PW2 deposed that he met the police in the hospital after about 30 minutes of their reaching hospital but police did not record his statement in writing.

He deposed that he left Delhi for his native village in UP on the next day of the accident with the dead body of deceased and returned after about 2 months, but could not tell the exact date and month of his return.
He contacted the IO at PS Narela, to enquire about his case repeatedly, when IO of the case was changed.
He deposed that he lodged a complaint against the IO with DCP office which is Ex. PW2/R3X.
PW2 denied all contrary suggestions regarding lodging of the complaint or false implication of the offending vehicle or being a planted witness to support the present false claim.
He denied the suggestion that he was not an eyewitness to the accident or that no accident took place with the said vehicle.

12. During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners heavily relied upon the criminal case record (which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/6 colly) in support of their case in order to bring home that the accident in question had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.

It has been contended that respondent no. 1 Sh. Badri Mandal was also charge-sheeted by police for offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC, which clearly establishes that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
13.
Per contra, it is contended on behalf of insurance company that PW2 Sh. Ram Raksha is a planted eyewitness of the accident.

It has been MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD:
10.11.2023 argued that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case.

Any liability of the insurance company has been denied on the ground that the insurance company has duly proved that the offending vehicle did not have a valid permit, for plying in Delhi, as on the date of accident.
It is contended that Insurance company is absolved from any liability in view of the statutory breach.
14. The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the DAR have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

As per DAR, the road accident in question took place on 01.01.2019 in front of BG Sirke Company A-5, Narela, Delhi, due to which, the deceased sustained fatal injuries and was declared dead at SRHC Hospital, Narela.

The offending vehicle Truck bearing registration no. HR74-0211 was seized from the accident spot and also respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle was admittedly the driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

sentences.text: He has been cross-examined at length to dispute his presence at spot and even to challenge his claimed employability with the construction company at whose construction site, the accident took place.

PW2 has categorically denied all contrary suggestions and affirmed the facts of the petition and averments in the chief-examination by way of MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 affidavit.

Despite having raised several suggestions and detailed cross- examination of PW2, who is a material witness, no contradictions that go to the root of occurrence of the accident in question, has been brought forth.

This is more so,
when respondents No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence to controvert the involvement of respondent no.1/driver or the alleged offending vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no.
HR74-0211.

Furthermore, it is an undisputed fact that case FIR No. 01/2019, dated 01.01.2019, U/s 279/304-A IPC was registered at PS Narela on the statement of SI Bijender with regard to the accident in question promptly and without any delay.

Not only this, respondent No.1/driver Sh.
Badri Mandal (accused in State case) has also been chargesheeted for offences punishable under Sections 279/304-A IPC.

Same would also point out towards rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1/driver.
15.

It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no. HR74-0211 by the respondent no.1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

sentences.text: 16. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of deceased victim prepared at SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, shows that he has been taken to said hospital on 01.01.2019.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in a motor vehicular accident.

Again,
there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents including insurance company.
Further, the postmortem report (which is part of DAR) also corroborates that cause of death of deceased was hemorrhagic shock consequent to injury to the chest and abdomen.
All the injuries were ante-mortem in nature, fresh in duration prior to death and caused by blunt force/surface impact.
The injuries as mentioned in the relevant column of external injuries of the said report, are also consistent with the injuries which are sustained in road traffic accident.
It is proved on record, by sufficient evidence as per law that the deceased succumbed to his injuries sustained in the road accident in question.

18. The petitioners who are claimants are the parents of deceased where petitioner no. 1 namely Sh.
Ram Laut is the father of deceased and petitioner no. 2 Smt. Sawari is the mother of deceased.

In the present case, the road accident in question has led to fatal injuries to the victim namely Suraj, who could not be saved even though, he was immediately taken to the nearby hospital i.e. SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi.
It is an undisputed material on record that deceased was unmarried at the time of accident.
Further, the postmortem report (which is part of DAR) also corroborates that cause of death of deceased was hemorrhagic shock consequent to injury to the chest and abdomen.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

19. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors., Vs. Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.

entities.text: Smt. Anjali & Ors., Vs. Lokendra Rathod & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16.

entities.text: Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit."
20. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance.
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

Per Contra, it has been contended by Ld. Counsel for insurance company that the petitioners have miserably failed to prove that the deceased MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD:
10.11.2023 was working and/or earning at the time of accident.
It is also assailed that there is no believable document or circumstance to support the claim of the petitioner that deceased was employed at Delhi.

Aadhar Card of the deceased Ex.PW1/5 has been relied upon to show that he was residing at his native place in UP and further that no employment or rental evidence as regards the earnings of deceased at Delhi, have been furnished.
It is prayed that the petition is liable to be dismissed as the petitioners have failed to show any dependency upon the deceased.
25. The petitioners have examined PW1/Father and PW2/brother of deceased.
The place of accident is the construction site where PW2 is stated to have been working.
PW2 has deposed that the deceased came to meet him at the accident spot and made a telephonic call to him.
It is deposed that PW2 who is the eye-witness, came out of a pit where he was working to meet his brother/deceased.

As per the testimony of PW2, the unfortunate accident occurred at the accident spot when the offending truck in question which was carrying construction material/bricks, hit the deceased with great force, being driven rashly and negligently by its driver.
It has further come in evidence that some unknown 4 to 5 persons took the then injured deceased to the nearby SRHC hospital in the ambulance.
No other co-worker has been examined by the petitioners to support their claim that the deceased was either working at the same place as that of PW2 or any other place in Delhi.

The petitioners have failed to lead any cogent evidence showing that MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19;
PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 deceased was working and earning in Delhi at the time of accident.
Moreover, PW1/Father of deceased during his cross-examination admitted that he did not have any documentary proof regarding the income/occupation of deceased.
The petitioners have failed to establish that deceased was working and earning in Delhi at the time of unfortunate accident in question.
Hence, the assessment of income of deceased is to be computed on the basis of minimum wages applicable in the State of Uttar Pradesh, during the relevant period.
The petitioners have filed copy of 8 th Class marksheet (Ex. PW1/7) of deceased which shows that deceased was 8th class pass.

Accordingly, it shall be appropriate to assess the monthly income of deceased as per applicability of minimum wages of a Non-Matriculate person applicable in the State of UP, as on the date of accident i.e. 01.01.2019.

The minimum wages of a non-matriculate person were Rs. 9,106/- per month in the State of UP, which is being taken as income of the deceased as on the date of accident i.e. 01.01.2019.
26.
In order to consider the age of deceased, the relevant documents are his Aadhaar Card and school marksheet of class 8 th wherein his recorded date of birth is 01.01.1998.
Date of accident being 01.01.2019, the age of deceased is taken as 21 years as on the date of accident.

Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Ld. Counsel for insurance company sought to avoid the liability of insurance company to pay the compensation amount on the ground that the offending vehicle was not having valid permit for State of Delhi at the time of accident in question.

In order to substantiate the said plea, insurance company has examined two witnesses Sh. Deepak, Transport Sub Inspector,
DTO-Cum-Secretary, RTA, District Sonepat, Haryana as R3W1 and Sh. Ajeet Kumar Lakra, Dy.

R3W1/1(colly).

He deposed that as per their record, the base permit was valid w.e.f. 12.02.2014 to 11.02.2019, however, National Permit authorization had expired on 11.02.2017 and it was renewed on 03.01.2019 and therefore, National Permit Authorization was not valid on the date of accident i.e.
01.01.2019 as there was a gap between the expiry and renewal of the same.
He further deposed that the authorization for the said permit was not valid as on the date of accident i.e. 01.01.2019 for the place of accident i.e. Narela.
He further deposed that the offending vehicle was not authorized to ply in Delhi at the time of accident.

sentences.text: 34. The other witness of the Insurance Company is R3W2 who has tendered his chief-examination by way of affidavit Ex. R3W2/A with the deposition that there was no valid and effective permit in respect of offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
He further deposed that despite notice u/o 12 Rule 8 CPC (Ex. R3W2/1) upon registered owner, he failed to produce any Permit.
He has relied upon copy of said notice as Ex. R3W2/1, postal receipt as Ex. R3W2/2 regarding dispatch of said notice and copy of insurance policy of offending vehicle as Ex. R3W2/3(colly).
Said witness has not been cross-examined at all by driver and registered owner despite grant of MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD: 10.11.2023 opportunity.
35. Respondents no. 1 & 2 did not challenge both the aforesaid witnesses.

The respondent no. 2 i.e.
registered owner, despite being put to notice U/o 12 rule 8 CPC ( Ex. R3W1/1), failed to bring on record any valid permit.
Both R1 and R2 have also failed to enter into witness box or to file any valid permit pertaining to offending vehicle in respect of Delhi, during the period in question.

Accordingly, R3/Insurance Company has duly discharged its onus to prove that there was a statutory breach as per provision U/s 149(2) of MV Act, and proved that the offending truck bearing registration no. HR74-0211 did not have a valid permit for Delhi, as on the date of accident.

36. At this juncture, it would be relevant to refer to the provision contained in Section 66 (1) of M.V Act which read as under:-
Necessity for Permits:-(1) No owner of a motor vehicle shall use or permit the use of the vehicle as a transport vehicle in any public place whether or not such vehicle is actually carrying any passengers or goods save in accordance with the conditions of a permit granted or countersigned by a Regional or State Transport Authority or any prescribed authority authorising him the use of the vehicle in that place in the manner in which the vehicle is being used.

37. It is quite clear from the bare perusal of the aforesaid provision that transport vehicle cannot be used in any public place, whether or not such MACP No.389/19; FIR No.01/19; PS. Narela DOD:
10.11.2023 vehicle is actually carrying any passengers or goods, save in accordance with the conditions of a permit granted by Regional or State Transport Authority.
Thus, there is clear violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy for want of valid permit in respect of offending vehicle as on the date of accident.

In these circumstances, having duly proved that there was a breach in terms and conditions of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle in question, on the part of insured i.e. respondent no. 2, therefore, insurance company is entitled to recovery rights against the respondents no. 1 & 2 jointly and severally.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.
